# Bitfroest.fs 0.0.49

Changes since the published version [0.0.40](https://github.com/s-a/Bitfroest.fs/releases/tag/v0.0.40), including all unreleased intermediate versions.

## Added

- **Help links.** The Help menu links to Microsoft Marketplace, GitHub, the product README, developer documentation and a new issue. Separators group product pages, documentation and issue reporting; licenses and acknowledgements appear last.
- **Select search matches.** Ctrl+B selects entries matching the current file-list search while preserving existing selections. The shortcut can be changed in the settings.
- **Show only search matches.** Ctrl+Shift+F limits the current file list to matching names. Escape clears the search and restores the full list while preserving selected entries. Filter state is kept separately for each folder tab, and the shortcut can be changed in the settings.
- **Optional copy verification.** The copy and move dialog includes "Compare file contents after copying", disabled by default. The choice is saved in `bitfroest.files.verifyAfterCopy` and reused for subsequent operations, including pasting files. File identity, size and safety checks remain enabled.
- **Folder history controls.** Back and forward arrows in each panel's Name column header navigate the current tab's folder history. Right-click either arrow to select a previously visited folder directly. Jumping to an earlier folder retains the forward history.
- **Copy paths with forward slashes.** The new "Copy full paths with forward slashes" command copies selected paths using `/` on Windows. The default shortcut is `Ctrl+Shift+Y`; existing path-copy commands retain their usual format.
- **Copy the current folder path.** Right-click the address bar's folder path to copy it to the clipboard. The tooltip shows the path and the mouse action; the status bar and a brief pulse on the path confirm a successful copy.
- Git context menus offer a read-only log for a selected file or folder in a detected repository, including through the Windows system context menu. The log shows a commit graph and changed files; double-click a changed file to compare committed versions in the VS Code diff editor.
- On Windows, Git file menus offer **Delete (Keep Local)** and **Delete and Add to Ignore List**. Both retain the local file and stage its removal from Git; the latter also adds an exact rule to the adjacent `.gitignore`. Neither creates a commit, and removal that would discard staged-only content is refused.

## Improved

- The delayed second-click rename shows a subtle left-to-right fill across the filename cell during its 650 ms delay. Cancelling the gesture removes the cue immediately; reduced-motion settings use a static highlight.
- Context menu hover highlighting no longer draws a border around the selected item. Keyboard focus remains visible.
- Double-clicking a folder shows a smaller loading ring inside that folder's icon. The source row remains visible until the directory read completes; failures and cancellation clear the ring. Other navigation methods do not animate the location star.
- **Symbolic link names.** Names of symbolic links to files and folders are underlined in directory listings and search results on Windows and Linux.
- **File-list search.** Names can be searched using complete phrases, including spaces. Typing after an input pause starts a new search; Ctrl+F starts a replacement query immediately with the next character. Search highlights update without rebuilding both file lists or changing selected entries. Sorting retains the search and scrolls the current match into view. Changing directories clears the search, filter and selected entries, including when navigating back or forward.
- **Active folder title.** The file manager window title follows the active folder.
- **Date sorting.** Columns combining a date and time sort chronologically, independently of their displayed format. This applies to modification, creation and access timestamps.
- **File conflict comparison.** A compact source-and-target view shows a shared filename once and marks equal known metadata in green. Exact byte and millisecond differences remain visible; missing metadata is never treated as equal. The dialog uses more of the available width and keeps frequent decisions in a fixed action footer.
- **Transfer dialog layout.** Source, destination and options are grouped with consistent spacing. Each checkbox has its own aligned row. Help for transfer options, filename extensions and filters is available in tooltips instead of inline paragraphs.
- **Destination filenames during transfers.** The "Set each destination filename" option explains when names are requested. Its dialog shows the original name, target folder and resulting filename, groups the transfer and skip actions, and uses the correct Copy or Move label. The original extension is retained when no new extension is entered.
- **File actions while folders load.** Copying, moving, packing, unpacking, renaming, deleting and creating entries no longer wait for unrelated directory reads to finish. Dialogs remain available during folder reads and refreshes. Confirmed operations take priority over pending list reads; interrupted lists resume afterward.
- **Fewer metadata queries on Windows.** Folder listings retrieve file sizes, timestamps, attributes and file identities in batches, avoiding separate metadata queries for each regular entry. This reduces the number of queries when opening or refreshing large folders, including supported SMB shares. Filesystems that do not support the batch query retain the existing read path.
- **Native folder icons on Linux.** Folder icon lookup now reads GIO custom-icon metadata and KDE `.directory` icon references through the native module. It resolves relative icon paths and inherited icon themes, with the existing icon lookup as a fallback. Windows retains native folder icons, including custom icons from `desktop.ini`.
- **Icon contrast.** Native file and folder icons receive a light or dark outline when needed for contrast against the row background. The outline adapts to selection and focus states while retaining the original icon colors.
- **Startup diagnostics.** Diagnostics now correlate host and webview startup, rendering readiness, focus changes and Git requests. On Windows, they also record native window visibility, bounds and maximization state to distinguish rendering failures from window restoration failures.
- **Release descriptions.** Version-tag builds check the matching release notes before installing dependencies or building the native module. Publication rechecks the notes and uses the version file as the GitHub release description.
- File lists use a new grid with aligned address and column headers. Text in the address row can be selected without triggering grid gestures. Active folder tabs use the standard tab background without an additional accent line.
- Left-button dragging starts immediately and copies the selected files after confirmation; Shift or Alt selects moving. Right-button dragging draws a selection rectangle from file rows or empty list space. Holding the right button still on a file for 400 ms prepares dragging, with a fill across the filename cells of the visible selection during the wait, and opens the move confirmation on drop.
- Drag previews show up to five selected rows with their icons and columns at partial opacity, plus the remaining count. The total selection count appears below the preview, outside the faded row edges. The grabbed row stays under the pointer, and the preview follows it without snapping to window edges or rebuilding when modifier keys change. The full selection is retained for the operation.
- Drag readiness and active dragging show white Material Symbols rings with a black outline behind the unchanged system pointer. Its arrow size and hotspot remain unchanged; no second arrow is drawn.

## Fixed

- A delayed file-paste response no longer starts a transfer after focus moves to the address bar or another text input.
- Opening a ZIP file from search results preserves the result tab and opens the archive in a separate folder tab.
- Favorites open only in the selected panel. Opposite-panel destinations and their configuration fields have been removed; previously saved destinations are ignored.
- Unchanged loading indicators in the opposite panel are no longer rebuilt when navigation activity updates.
- Rapid mouse-button changes no longer allow a stale native file drag to overlap a pointer preview. Pressing both buttons cancels the gesture without starting a transfer.
- File clipboard commands no longer appear over unrelated controls and dialogs. Text fields retain their editing menu.
- The location menu opens visibly from the star or Git icon in either file panel.
- Refreshing a folder reads only that panel’s folder. When both panels show the same folder, one read updates both lists.
- The address header stays fixed to the panel viewport when columns are resized, reordered or scrolled. The refresh control stays at the right edge with equal top and bottom spacing.
- The refresh symbol is centered inside its button using its actual outline rather than the font's oversized bounding box.
- Folder navigation holds existing column widths while loading and runs the grid's content autosizing once after the final directory response. Partial listings do not resize columns.
- Normal deletion requests the recycle bin for local entries; Shift+Delete and Shift+F8 request permanent deletion. The previous `bitfroest.files.deleteToTrash` setting is no longer used.
- On Windows, deleting network files with the recycle-bin option requests confirmation before permanently deleting network targets. Local targets retain the selected deletion mode.
- Delete commands in the file context menu use the captured selection and reject a changed tab. Shift-delete requests permanent deletion.
- Delayed inline rename is cancelled when focus or the selected file changes, preventing an unintended rename.
- Inline rename preserves text selection and editing when its text context menu opens. Focus loss keeps the proposed name; clicking outside confirms a valid change, Enter confirms and Escape discards it. Text selection and dragging inside the input no longer open or transfer the file.
- Folder deletion no longer recursively lists or reads the selected folder before invoking deletion. Already displayed entries can be deleted while a directory listing is still loading. Target identity and link checks remain active.
- Directory preparation retries a transient zero-timestamp response once when the other recorded directory metadata is unchanged. Persistent timestamp differences and changed directory identities still stop preparation.
- Rejected native copies retain the expected and observed source identifiers, size and timestamps in their error details, including the specific fields that differ. The source validation remains enforced before copying.
- The parent-directory row displays `..` and highlights when files are dragged over it. After transfer confirmation, its immediate destination listing is reread even when cached, so existing filenames trigger the conflict dialog. Transfer planning uses separate working data, keeping unconfirmed moves out of the visible file list during redraws.
- Windows file clipboard operations support NTFS network shares that provide a 64-bit file index but reject the extended identity query. Identity checks remain active. Access failures, unknown filesystems and missing identities still stop the operation. Clipboard error reports now retain native error codes and operation details.
- Moving a file after folder cache eviction no longer rejects a restored inactive tab as a foreign folder. Unprepared folder changes and unrelated paths remain blocked; rejected folder paths are included in error details.
- Temporary copy files retain their intended destination filename and extension, making any retained copy data identifiable if recovery is needed.
- Copy and move operations close the staging file's verification handle before removing its temporary directory, preventing directory-not-empty cleanup failures caused by a still-open handle.
- Successful Windows copies to SMB shares no longer fail with "The copied destination could not be matched to the operation handle" when the server finalizes timestamps after writing finishes. Destination identity checks remain active.
- Late folder and archive read results no longer replace the state of a confirmed file operation. Tab changes during transfer planning retain the last confirmed file contents.
- Native packages exclude local dependency and build directories. Native builds and packaging reject modules containing embedded user-profile paths.
- Folder navigation in either panel no longer waits for a directory read in the other panel. Background reads complete in their original tabs without moving keyboard focus. Path entry, file viewing and opening a terminal remain available during reads.
- Concurrent directory reads retain both panels' file listings. A slow read no longer evicts a newly visible folder when the cache is full or clears a newer listing after a folder has been replaced.
- Inline file renaming retains the original extension when the new name contains no dot. An explicitly entered extension replaces the original one. Name validation and collision checks use the resulting full filename; folder names are unaffected.
- Invalid Git progress messages no longer interrupt the file list or prevent native icons from appearing after startup or a refresh.
- Filesystem icon requests that finish after the icon cache has been cleared no longer repopulate it with stale results.
- Folder refreshes request updated native icons and reject replies from an earlier view generation.
- Windows window-maximization failures now report the correct operation instead of the unrelated "Native desktop association failed" message, with additional diagnostic details.
- Compact folder history arrows remain aligned with the filename text without shifting the Name column heading.
- Windows startup checks whether a restored Commander window is actually hidden before enabling file actions. If the window is uniquely identified and remains hidden on a second check, the extension reopens its own panel through the normal new-window path. Saved folder tabs and their active positions are retained. The recovery is part of the extension and does not modify VS Code application files.
- Window ownership checks are read-only, scoped to a temporary title identifier, and cancelled when the panel closes. Visible, minimized, ambiguous and unrelated windows do not trigger recovery. A replacement panel cannot repeat the restoration recovery.
- Delayed navigation remains associated with the original panel and tab. Navigating in one panel no longer clears or redraws an unchanged listing in the other panel.
- File-list totals display readable size units.
- Automatic column sizing keeps extension and size columns fitted to their own headings and values, without widening them to accommodate the address row.
- Automatically sized columns retain the grid's built-in spacing after content measurement, including date and time columns.
- Folder navigation preserves the file grid and its column widths, avoiding repeated sizing animations when the required widths stay the same. Automatic sizing still adapts to changed content and preserves manually resized columns.
- The file manager launcher uses only a folder icon in the status bar. Detached editor windows also offer a folder button in the editor title bar, including image previews and other non-text editors.
- The file manager's status-bar entry and opening commands remain unavailable until its initial shortcut configuration and renderer acknowledgement are complete. They remain unavailable during panel startup until the browser and host are ready. Direct opening requests wait for initialization and cannot create duplicate windows.
- Focus refreshes and other messages arriving immediately after a fresh panel reports readiness now wait for the host's readiness transition. The same synchronization applies after a panel document reload, preventing requests from being discarded during that transition.
- Closing the extension during initialization prevents delayed window creation. Startup diagnostics remain accessible if initialization fails. The initialization tooltip is available in German and English.

## Known limitations

- Clipboard acknowledgement after cancelling a multi-directory move remains under verification.
- Recursive deletion uses the host filesystem API without internal per-file progress. Cancellation is checked before the deletion call; an active recursive deletion cannot be interrupted through this API.
- Windows remains the primary supported platform. Published Windows and Linux packages target x64 processors.
- Linux supports the implemented native integrations and portable file operations. The system file clipboard and Windows shell context menu are unavailable. Linux packages target Ubuntu 24.04 or a compatible newer runtime.
- Native folder icons on Linux require GIO, GdkPixbuf and installed image loaders. SVG icons require the librsvg loader. Minimal systems may need the Ubuntu packages `libglib2.0-0t64`, `libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0`, `librsvg2-common` and `shared-mime-info`.
- Batched directory metadata retrieval is Windows-specific. Linux retains its existing Node.js directory-reading behavior. The actual speed improvement on network shares depends on the server, connection and filesystem; no fixed speedup is guaranteed.
- macOS is not officially supported.
- Drag previews and pointer rings have headless behavior coverage. Their native appearance across display scales and pointer schemes has not been verified.
- This is beta software. File operations modify real data; evaluation should use test data or a current, restorable backup.
- This update waits for the file manager's own initialization. It does not wait for every installed extension to activate and does not establish a fix for every possible blank or unresponsive window failure.
- The targeted recovery of hidden native Windows windows has limited scope. It does not verify rendered pixels or recover failed VS Code webview service-worker initialization.
- Reload or restart VS Code after installing the update to activate the new extension code. VS Code application files are not modified.
